# CI Workflow Guidance

## Windows Build Contract

- `workflows/build-sakura.yml` builds the x64 `{Debug, Release}` matrix; both configurations build with `build-sln.bat`.
- The workflow runs the test suite before creating the installer. Release jobs package and upload one AVX-baseline `sakura.exe`; AVX2 and AVX-512F/BW implementations are selected inside that binary at runtime.
- Pull requests build and test both MSVC configurations, but skip CHM, BmpTools, the installer, ZIP creation, and production uploads. Each matrix job uploads a `test-results-<platform>-<config>` artifact (googletest XML plus the copied trigger event) for `workflows/test-results.yml`.
- The MSBuild job uses `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` and starts with an explicit prerequisite validator. `build-vcpkg-msvc` is the strict dependency; `build-vcpkg-mingw` is experimental and advisory, matching the MinGW workflow contract.
- After GitHub Packages is configured, each MSBuild matrix job explicitly runs `py -3 tools/build/sakura_build.py package restore sakura_app --context <context>` before invoking MSBuild. The vcpkg prerequisite job warms binary-cache entries only; it cannot provide the runner-local manifest-hashed active package root, and normal project evaluation must never perform an implicit restore.
- `SAKURA_GENERATE_ASSEMBLY_LISTINGS` is a job-level env on `build`, not scoped to the MSBuild step alone: `zipArtifacts.bat` and the Upload Asm step both need to see the same value the MSBuild step used. It resolves to `1` only for `matrix.config == 'Release'` on non-`pull_request` triggers (integration-branch push or `workflow_dispatch`); Debug never needs listing I/O, and `pull_request` Release builds leave it `0` since they never publish the Asm artifact.
- This setting does more than emit `.asm` files: it also serializes LTCG codegen (`/CGTHREADS:1`). Issue #43 Phase 2b's verified two-pair comparison found that turning Listings off reduced the Release MSBuild step by 34.9-40.6% (pooled 37.8%), roughly 9-11 minutes. Link was the only reproducible driver; CL and Exec deltas changed sign between pairs. `zipArtifacts.bat` treats the Asm archive as optional (skips the `.asm` copy and zip instead of failing `copyRequired`'s missing-file check) when the value isn't `1`/`true`, and the workflow's Upload Asm step mirrors that with `env.SAKURA_GENERATE_ASSEMBLY_LISTINGS == '1'`.
- Do not replace CI's solution build with `build-dev.bat`, and do not narrow the required full headless suite solely for speed. The one deliberate exception is a same-repository `feature/*` PR targeting `develop`: it may restore the exact-base coverage map and run its selected `tests1` suites plus the fixed smoke suite. Every separately registered component test executable and pytest still run with the ordinary headless filter. A cache miss, bad provenance, unknown diff, unmapped source, selection error, or any non-feature/fork/promotion PR must retain the normal full headless filter.
- `workflows/coverage-map.yml` is reusable only from a successful trusted `develop` push after the full MSBuild matrix. It receives the short-lived Debug `tests1.exe`/PDB bundle, collects suite-level OpenCppCoverage fragments in eight shards, emits compact validated partial maps, and saves only the final JSON map under the exact `tia-map-windows-x64-<base-sha>-<schema>` key. PR jobs use `actions/cache/restore` only; never allow a PR, `workflow_run`, or an untrusted artifact to write this cache. Map-only failures publish nothing and leave the next feature PR on the full-suite fallback.
- SonarCloud analysis was removed in #112 after the evidence showed it had never produced a result in this fork: zero successful runs in the last 50 `sonarscan.yml` invocations, an empty SonarCloud project, no PR decoration, and two independent breakages (a rejected `SONAR_TOKEN` and Build Wrapper compile commands naming a VS2022 Enterprise `cl.exe` path absent on the scan runner). Do not reintroduce a scanner without an owner-confirmed working token and a compile-commands plan. The one useful by-product, the "Test Results" check, is now published by `workflows/test-results.yml`, a `workflow_run` consumer of the Release `test-results-*` artifact with the same success and same-repository guard the Sonar consumer used. Because the Debug leg's instrumented CoverageTest existed only to feed Sonar coverage, `CMakeLists.txt` registers `UnitTest` for both configurations when OpenCppCoverage is absent (the hosted build jobs no longer install it); a machine with OpenCppCoverage installed keeps the instrumented Debug CoverageTest and a Release-only UnitTest, so `tests1` runs exactly once per configuration in both worlds.

## Other Workflows

- `workflows/build-on-msys2.yml` owns the experimental MinGW build and repeated test run.
- Encoding, Python, cppcheck, and Doxygen workflows are separate checks. The required build, cppcheck, and Doxygen workflows have no path filters so a docs-only PR cannot leave a required context expected forever; the advisory MinGW workflow retains its path filters.
- `workflows/cppcheck.yml` caches cppcheck's analyzer information (`--cppcheck-build-dir`, #112). That flag is not a compiler cache and must not be reasoned about as one: cppcheck stores one analysis result per translation unit and re-emits the cached findings, so a hit reports exactly what a miss would, and it additionally restores the whole-program checks (`unusedFunction`, `ctunullpointer`, `ctuuninitvar`) that `-j` otherwise disables. Measured against `sakura_core/sakura.vcxproj` with cppcheck 2.21.0, the build MSYS2 installs: 609s uncached with 6280 findings, 599s cold with 7558, 18s warm with 7558, the cold and warm XML byte-identical. Two consequences are deliberate. The uploaded artifact now carries roughly 1278 additional whole-program findings, which is safe only because the job passes no `--error-exitcode` and therefore never gates on findings - do not add one without re-triaging that set first. And the cache is restored on every event but saved only when `github.event_name != 'pull_request'`: a pull-request run's entry is scoped to its own ref and readable by no other run, while the repository-wide 10 GiB cache quota was already 8.46 GiB full (81 `msys2` entries) when this landed. A pull request therefore restores the default branch's entry and re-analyzes only the translation units it changed. The key carries the resolved cppcheck version so a rolling `mingw-w64-x86_64-cppcheck` upgrade cannot resurrect another analyzer's results; the version reaches the key through a workspace file rather than `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` because the MSYS2 shell would have to append to a Windows path and this is a required check. `src/test/py/test_cppcheck_analyzer_cache.py` pins the workflow path against the directory `run-cppcheck.bat` computes, because drift between them makes every run a cold run without turning anything red.
- Push workflows target the protected `main` and `develop` branches. Normal feature, fix, and Dependabot pull requests target `develop`; only same-repository `develop` and `hotfix/*` branches may target `main`.
- `workflows/develop-issue-closure.yml` exists because that branch policy disables GitHub's own closing keywords: GitHub applies `Closes #N` only when a pull request merges into the default branch, which is `main`, so no ordinary pull request here can ever auto-close its issue. Verified by PR #109, which carried `Closes #15`, merged into `develop`, and left Issue #15 open. The workflow resolves the keywords from the merged pull request's title and body through `.github/scripts/close_referenced_issues.py`, then comments the merge commit and closes each issue with `gh`. Two divergences from GitHub's behavior are deliberate: only references naming this repository are closed (`#N`, `GH-N`, and this repository's own qualified and URL forms), with a cross-repository reference logged and left alone so the fork-only boundary cannot be crossed by automation; and keywords inside HTML comments, fenced code blocks, and inline code spans are ignored, with the keyword required to share a line with its reference, so the pull request template's own Japanese commentary closes nothing. Fork and Dependabot pull requests receive a read-only token whatever the permissions block says, so the job reports those events and stands down rather than failing. Its status messages deliberately avoid the filter/skip vocabulary that `tools/build/sakura_build_lib/semantic_inventory.py` counts as `test.filtered_or_skipped` in every `.github` file: the first revision of this workflow said "skipping issue closure" and failed `inventory semantic --strict` with five new findings. That gate exists to catch real test exclusion, so the wording changed instead of the baseline, and a test reads the rule's own pattern out of the scanner source to keep the workflow clear of it. `src/test/py/test_develop_issue_closure.py` owns both the parser behavior and the workflow contract; change them together. It sits in `src/test/py` rather than beside the other workflow-contract tests because the CTest `pytest` target runs from the repository root under pytest's default `norecursedirs`, which skips any directory named `build`: `tools/build/tests` is therefore never collected in CI, and a contract test placed there would silently never run.
- A branch-creation push reports an all-zero `github.event.before` and has no content diff. The encoding check treats that event as a successful no-op rather than scanning the historical baseline, which contains pre-existing UTF-8-no-BOM files; pull-request/base-SHA checks remain authoritative for changed files.
- `workflows/release-promotion.yml` promotes only a canonical tag whose commit is reachable from `main`, has a successful required source gate, and matches the tag's non-merge build revision. It calls `build-sakura.yml` with the exact source SHA, checks executable/installer hashes and version metadata, installs and opens the packaged payload in an isolated smoke job, then grants `contents: write` only to the final draft-and-publish job. Do not move publication permission or artifact execution into an earlier job.
- Promotion helpers check out `github.workflow_sha`, not the target tag. The resolver and reusable package workflow may consume the target only as an immutable data/source reference; smoke and publication must never execute helper code supplied by that target checkout.

## Workflow Changes

- Preserve the distinction between local speed optimizations and release/CI completeness.
- Keep action permissions and downloaded tooling narrowly scoped. Pin or update actions deliberately and retain any existing commit pin where the workflow uses one.
- Verify YAML structure and inspect every changed matrix branch; a condition that works for Release must not accidentally add work to Debug jobs.
- Repository PowerShell scripts follow `.gitattributes`: UTF-16LE with BOM and CRLF in the working tree. Preserve that encoding when adding workflow helpers; Git converts the committed representation to UTF-8.
